spans.text: Underground Area, Frankfurt, White Zone.
Dim and damp, the air carries the musty stench of mold. Kalina's group advances through the narrow ventilation shaft in a fixed order.
The surroundings are eerily quiet, with only the occasional drip of water and the hum of unknown industrial-control machinery.
The ground is thick with mud; they have to move with extra care to avoid making noise.
Miss Kalina...
Tokarev calls out softly, pointing at the ground.
What is it?
Miss Kalina, look. This muddy water must have been accumulating for a very long time. But the deeper we go, the thinner the layer of mud becomes. That doesn't make sense.
The environment in here is relatively stable, and the overall terrain is flat, with no noticeable slope.
So logically, this entire route should be uniformly muddy. Yet the farther in we go, the cleaner it gets.
You mean... someone cleaned up? Covered up footprints and other traces?
Tokarev nods. She walks over to the wall and wipes away a layer of surface dust with her hand.
And look here. This section of wall isn't the same as when we first came in. The material is reinforced concrete with much higher strength.
The internal structure has also changed—from a single-layer design to a layered structure resistant to bunker-busting munitions. That's clearly beyond the safety requirements of a ventilation shaft.
So that means...?
Oh~ Come take a look over here!
Six12 seems to have discovered something. Kalina and Tokarev exchange a glance, nod to each other, and move over with the other two Dolls.
Kalina's group gathers where Six12 is standing. In the direction she is pointing, there is a signboard stained with muddy water.
A subway station... entrance. It's hard to read. The facilities around here are all heavily worn.
But if this were just an abandoned subway station, would there really be a need for military-grade fortifications?
Mm. The situation is becoming fairly clear.
Combined with what Tokarev has observed earlier, this should be part of Frankfurt's Cold War–era civil defense network. It looks like it was abandoned even before the war.
Underground facilities like this usually aren't marked with precise locations on modern maps, which makes them difficult to track down.
The underground network branches in all directions. Finding the Commander won't be easy...
Let's follow the route ahead and check it first. Maybe the Commander left some kind of marker.
Tokarev exchanges looks with the other Dolls; they all nod, then form a protective formation around Kalina as they proceed to move deeper into the subway station.
Every Doll keeps their eyes peeled, but none of the expected markers appear along the way.
We're going pretty deep, aren't we? Would the Commander really be in a place like this?
C14's apprehension is understandable. The deeper the team goes, the darker the tunnel becomes.
Stop. There's no way forward.
The group halts. Tokarev and Six12 move up to check. There is almost no illumination here. Only a few emergency lights glow with a deep, ghostly green in the darkness.
When Tokarev approaches, she realizes what's blocking them—a military-grade security door with a digital access lock.
This is a military security door. The steel plating is extremely thick. There's almost no chance of forcing it open from the outside...
Wooooo—
Before Tokarev can finish, a piercing, continuous alarm suddenly blares.
In an instant, every emergency light in the underground passage snaps on. The pitch-black space is flooded with blood-red warning lights.
That long, droning alarm sounds like a death knell tolling.
What's going on?!
Along with the alarm, Tokarev hears mechanical movement from above.
She looks up, and several steel gates suddenly slam down from the ceiling...
Directly onto Kalina!
Miss Kalina!
Tokarev reacts in a flash, diving to her left towards Kalina, hauling her several meters away.
Whoa! What just happened?!
Before CZ-805 can even process the situation, she sees red warning lights flashing—and muzzle flashes erupting from several gun barrels.
Modified autonomous Dolls pour out of hidden wall panels and open fire on Kalina's group without hesitation.
Enemy contact! Find cover nearby! Prepare to engage!
Kalina and Tokarev take cover behind a section of wall. Tokarev draws her weapon and returns fire.
The other Dolls each find their own cover, relying on solid combat training to stabilize the situation.
Yet these autonomous Dolls are like endless sandbags—knock one down, and another rises to take its place.
The Commander...? Why would the Commander attack us?
I don't remember anyone doing anything out of line just now... why?
The sudden turn of events puts Kalina on edge and deepens her confusion.
The idea that the Commander would attack them is something she simply cannot comprehend.
Miss Kalina! Miss Kalina!
Can you hear me?
Pulled out of her thoughts by Tokarev's voice, Kalina turns and sees her standing behind.
Stay close to me! I'll escort you to the security door!
Huh? What did you say?
These autonomous Dolls and the sudden steel gates... are both only meant to delay intruders, not eliminate them.
Now that the alarm is sounding, the Commander must be aware of what's happening. Relying on these measures to stall for time means that...
That... the Commander probably prepared another exit! Not knowing the intruders are us, the Commander will withdraw according to the original plan.
And then we'll completely lose our chance to find them!
So we'll clear the way for you. You go on and find the Commander!
But the enemies' firepower is too strong! You—
Six12! CZ-805! Prepare to fall back and tighten the formation!
Roger!
Before Kalina can say anything more, Tokarev's voice rings out again.
Miss C14! Please cover us! I'm going to hack the electronic lock!
Understood!
Before Kalina can fully grasp what's happening, Tokarev grabs her arm and, seizing the moment when the autonomous Dolls run out of ammo, drags her toward the security door.
The other three Dolls cluster around them, shielding Kalina with their own bodies and protecting her from stray rounds.
Even through the alarms and gunfire, Kalina can hear the dull thuds of bullets striking Doll frames.
Each sound lands heavily in her chest.
Miss Kalina, remember what you said to me up there?
"If every problem could be solved easily, there must be a carefully crafted lie behind it all."
Now is the moment to put that to the test. I ask you—please, you must see the Commander.
Not just for yourself, but for us—for those of us who, because of protocol, couldn't stand beside the Commander in the final battle...
...I don't remember who asked me, but someone once did. They asked whether I ever regretted fighting for the Commander, regretted following the Commander through all this suffering. Whether I ever—
...resented the Commander.
My answer was no.
Before I met the Commander, I didn't even understand what love was, or hatred, or hope, or regret.
I wasn't even given the right to possess such emotions, let alone discuss them.
It was the Commander who gave me all of this. It was the Commander who told me that I, too, had the right—the right to a sense of self, to dignity, to emotions.
We're not like the AR Team or Task Force Defy, who clearly know what they're fighting for.
To be honest, our understanding of Paradeus is almost nonexistent compared to theirs.
We're not fighting for justice or lofty ideals either. I even doubt whether I truly understand what "justice" and "righteousness" mean on a grand scale in this war.
We... fight only for the Commander.
Because of the Commander, we take up arms. As long as the Commander gives the order, we'll charge ahead without hesitation.
Before meeting the Commander, we would do the same—because we were cheap tools that obeyed orders.
After meeting the Commander, we still do the same—because now we understand what love is, what it means to choose for ourselves...
...and what "self-respect" means for a Doll!
Please... convey our feelings to the Commander as well!
Miss Kalina! Stay strong!
We want to do something for you—both for you and the Commander.
That's right! Leave this place to us. You just need to keep moving forward.
What Tokarev wants to say is exactly what we want to tell the Commander too!
Boom!!
Suddenly, a shell detonates near Kalina and the others, catching her completely off guard.
In the violent shockwave, most of her hearing cuts out, replaced by relentless ringing.
Nausea washes over her as her head starts spinning.
She lifts her head with great difficulty—and sees Six12 and CZ-805, whose frames have suffered massive damage absorbing most of the blast for her.
Even so, they continue to shield Kalina tightly behind them.
Six12!
Everything around her is bathed in red. Kalina can't hear anything. And they can no longer answer her.
Tokarev sees it when she looks back, but says nothing—she forcibly turns away and speeds up her hacking.
Then C14, moving in to protect Tokarev and Kalina, is pierced through the abdomen by a closing mechanical unit.
Before she falls, C14 presses her sniper rifle against the machine's head and fires at point-blank range...
Kalina can't hear the gunshot, but she sees the instant C14 pulls the trigger, the sniper rifle explodes because the muzzle is completely blocked...
After the blast, both of them collapse.
She wants to say something, but she can't even hear her own voice.
The ringing in her ears is like a demon unleashed in the mortal world, tormenting her with a low hum that could drive anyone mad.
Then she feels someone helping her up. She turns her head—
In that final moment, all she sees is Tokarev's gentle smile.
Tokarev's lips seem to whisper something. Kalina can't hear it, but she tries desperately to read her lips.
After that, Kalina is gently pushed through the door. The heavy door closes behind her.
In an instant, the world plunges into darkness—cut off completely from everything outside.
